coverage: Both full English editions. INFERNO (chapters 1-34) is authored; Purgatorio (35-67) and Paradiso (68-100) are in progress. Named people, gods, angels, devils, personified powers, named monsters and named peoples. Places, rivers, mountains and book titles are not cast, except where a river of the underworld is treated as a power.

entities.name: Dante
entities.body: The poet who is also the pilgrim of his own poem. He names himself exactly once in the whole Comedy, when Beatrice calls him by name in the earthly paradise.

entities.name: Virgil
entities.body: The Roman poet of the Aeneid, sent to guide Dante through Hell and Purgatory; a soul of Limbo, saved from damnation but not from exclusion. Longfellow spells him Virgilius.

entities.name: Beatrice
entities.body: The Florentine woman Dante loved, now among the blessed; she sends Virgil to his aid and takes over as his guide in the earthly paradise and through Heaven.

entities.name: Statius
entities.body: The Roman poet of the Thebaid, who joins the travellers in Purgatory and reveals that Virgil’s own verses converted him.

entities.name: Lucifer
entities.body: The emperor of the kingdom of grief, fixed in ice at the centre of the earth; also called Dis, Satan and Beelzebub.

entities.name: Charon
entities.body: The ancient ferryman with wheels of flame about his eyes, who carries the damned across Acheron.

entities.name: Minos
entities.body: The judge of the damned, who winds his tail about himself to sentence each soul to its circle.

entities.name: Cerberus
entities.body: The three-throated dog who howls over the gluttons in the rain.

entities.name: Plutus
entities.body: The hoarse-voiced guardian of the fourth circle, where the misers and spendthrifts roll their weights.

entities.name: Phlegyas
entities.body: The boatman who ferries Dante and Virgil across the marsh of Styx.

entities.name: Megaera
entities.body: One of the three Furies on the tower of Dis.

entities.name: Alecto
entities.body: One of the three Furies on the tower of Dis.

entities.name: Tisiphone
entities.body: One of the three Furies on the tower of Dis.

entities.name: Medusa
entities.body: The Gorgon the Furies call for, whose face would turn Dante to stone.

entities.name: The Minotaur
entities.body: The bull-man of Crete, who guards the descent into the circle of violence.

entities.name: Chiron
entities.body: The centaur who raised Achilles, chief of the troop that patrols the river of blood.

entities.name: Nessus
entities.body: The centaur who died for Deianira and now guides the travellers along the boiling river.

entities.name: Pholus
entities.body: A centaur of the river bank, full of wrath.

entities.name: The Harpies
entities.body: The bird-women who nest in the wood of the suicides.

entities.name: Geryon
entities.body: The monster with an honest face and a scorpion’s tail, who carries the travellers down to the eighth circle.

entities.name: The Malebranche
entities.body: The demon squad of the fifth ditch, who hook the barrators out of the boiling pitch.

entities.name: Malacoda
entities.body: The captain of the Malebranche, who lies to Virgil about the broken bridge.

entities.name: Barbariccia
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche, put in charge of the squad of ten.

entities.name: Alichino
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Calcabrina
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Cagnazzo
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Libicocco
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Draghignazzo
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Ciriatto
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche, tusked like a boar.

entities.name: Graffiacane
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Farfarello
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Rubicante
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Scarmiglione
entities.body: A demon of the Malebranche.

entities.name: Nimrod
entities.body: The giant of Babel, whose gibberish no one can understand; his tower is why the world has many tongues.

entities.name: Ephialtes
entities.body: A giant who warred against the gods, bound in chains at the pit’s edge.

entities.name: Briareus
entities.body: A giant of the war against the gods, named but not seen.

entities.name: Antaeus
entities.body: The unbound giant who lifts the travellers down to the frozen lake.

entities.name: Tityus
entities.body: A giant named among those the travellers do not want to be handed to.

entities.name: Typhoeus
entities.body: A giant named among those the travellers do not want to be handed to.

entities.name: The Old Man of Crete
entities.body: The great statue inside Mount Ida, cracked and weeping, whose tears make the rivers of Hell.

entities.name: Fortune
entities.body: The ministering power Virgil defends, who turns the goods of the world from one people to another.

entities.name: Homer
entities.body: The sovereign poet, first of the four who meet Virgil in Limbo.

entities.name: Horace
entities.body: The Roman satirist, one of the four poets of Limbo.

entities.name: Ovid
entities.body: The Roman poet of the Metamorphoses, one of the four poets of Limbo.

entities.name: Lucan
entities.body: The Roman poet of the Pharsalia, one of the four poets of Limbo.

entities.name: Electra
entities.body: Dardanus’s mother, seen among the great souls of Limbo.

entities.name: Hector
entities.body: Troy’s defender, seen among the great souls of Limbo.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: The founder of the Roman line, seen among the great souls of Limbo; his journey to the dead is Dante’s precedent.

entities.name: Camilla
entities.body: The warrior maiden of the Aeneid, who died for Italy.

entities.name: Penthesilea
entities.body: The Amazon queen, seen among the great souls of Limbo.

entities.name: Latinus
entities.body: The Latin king, seated with his daughter in Limbo.

entities.name: Lavinia
entities.body: Latinus’s daughter, seated beside him in Limbo.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.body: The Brutus who drove out Tarquin and founded the Roman republic, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.body: Caesar’s assassin, chewed in Lucifer’s mouth at the centre of Hell.

entities.name: Tarquin
entities.body: The last king of Rome, driven out by Brutus.

entities.name: Lucretia
entities.body: A Roman matron seen among the great souls of Limbo.

entities.name: Julia
entities.body: Caesar’s daughter and Pompey’s wife, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Marcia
entities.body: Cato’s wife, seen in Limbo; Virgil invokes her when asking Cato’s leave in Purgatory.

entities.name: Cornelia
entities.body: The mother of the Gracchi, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Saladin
entities.body: The Sultan of Egypt, seated alone and apart in Limbo.

entities.name: The master of those who know
entities.body: Aristotle, seated in the philosophical family of Limbo; the poem names him only by that title.

entities.name: Socrates
entities.body: The Athenian philosopher, closest to Aristotle in Limbo.

entities.name: Plato
entities.body: The Athenian philosopher, closest to Aristotle in Limbo.

entities.name: Democritus
entities.body: The philosopher who attributes the world to chance.

entities.name: Diogenes
entities.body: A philosopher of Limbo.

entities.name: Anaxagoras
entities.body: A philosopher of Limbo.

entities.name: Thales
entities.body: A philosopher of Limbo.

entities.name: Zeno
entities.body: A philosopher of Limbo.

entities.name: Empedocles
entities.body: A philosopher of Limbo.

entities.name: Heraclitus
entities.body: A philosopher of Limbo.

entities.name: Dioscorides
entities.body: The great collector of the properties of plants.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The singer of myth, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Cicero
entities.body: The Roman orator, seen in Limbo. Longfellow spells him Tully.

entities.name: Livy
entities.body: The Roman historian, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Seneca
entities.body: The Roman moralist, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Euclid
entities.body: The geometer, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Ptolemy
entities.body: The astronomer, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Galen
entities.body: The physician, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Hippocrates
entities.body: The physician, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Avicenna
entities.body: The Persian physician and philosopher, seen in Limbo.

entities.name: Averroes
entities.body: The Arab philosopher who wrote the great Commentary on Aristotle.

entities.name: Semiramis
entities.body: The Assyrian queen who made lust lawful, first of the carnal sinners named.

entities.name: Ninus
entities.body: Semiramis’s husband, whom she succeeded.

entities.name: Dido
entities.body: The queen of Carthage who killed herself for love and broke faith with Sychaeus’s ashes.

entities.name: Sychaeus
entities.body: Dido’s dead husband, whose ashes she broke faith with.

entities.name: Cleopatra
entities.body: The Egyptian queen, among the carnal sinners.

entities.name: Helen
entities.body: The woman for whose sake the Trojan war was fought.

entities.name: Achilles
entities.body: The Greek hero who at the last fought against Love.

entities.name: Paris
entities.body: The Trojan who carried Helen away.

entities.name: Tristan
entities.body: The lover of romance, among the carnal sinners.

entities.name: Francesca
entities.body: Francesca da Rimini, who tells Dante how she and her husband’s brother were carried away by a book, and were killed for it.

entities.name: Lancelot
entities.body: The knight whose story Francesca and her companion were reading.

entities.name: Ciacco
entities.body: A Florentine glutton who prophesies the city’s coming strife.

entities.name: Farinata
entities.body: Farinata degli Uberti, the Ghibelline leader who rises out of his burning tomb and speaks of Florence.

entities.name: Guido
entities.body: Guido Cavalcanti, the poet and Dante’s friend, asked after by his father in the tombs of the heretics.

entities.name: Frederick
entities.body: The emperor Frederick the Second, named as lying among the Epicureans, and whose leaden capes are a byword.

entities.name: The Cardinal
entities.body: Ottaviano degli Ubaldini, named only by his office among the heretics.

entities.name: Anastasius
entities.body: The pope whose tomb Dante passes, said to have been led from the true path.

entities.name: Photinus
entities.body: The deacon said to have led Pope Anastasius astray.

entities.name: Alexander
entities.body: A tyrant boiling in the river of blood, named beside Dionysius.

entities.name: Alexander
entities.body: Alexander the Great, whose army in India saw flames fall unbroken from the sky.

entities.name: Dionysius
entities.body: The tyrant of Syracuse, boiling in the river of blood.

entities.name: Azzolino
entities.body: Ezzelino da Romano, the black-haired tyrant in the river of blood.

entities.name: Obizzo
entities.body: Obizzo d’Este, the fair-haired tyrant in the river of blood, killed by his own stepson.

entities.name: Attila
entities.body: The scourge of the earth, deep in the boiling blood.

entities.name: Pyrrhus
entities.body: A tyrant in the boiling blood.

entities.name: Sextus
entities.body: A tyrant in the boiling blood.

entities.name: Rinier da Corneto
entities.body: A highway robber, boiling in the river of blood.

entities.name: Rinier Pazzo
entities.body: A highway robber, boiling in the river of blood.

entities.name: The one who held both keys
entities.body: Frederick the Second’s chancellor, who turned his master’s heart softly in locking and unlocking, and killed himself when envy turned the court against him. He is the speaking tree of the wood of the suicides, and the canto never gives his name.

entities.name: Lano
entities.body: A Sienese squanderer, hunted through the wood by black hounds.

entities.name: Jacopo da Sant’Andrea
entities.body: A Paduan squanderer, torn apart by the hounds in the wood of the suicides.

entities.name: The Florentine who hanged himself
entities.body: The bush who speaks last in the wood, from the city that changed its patron saint to the Baptist.

entities.name: Capaneus
entities.body: One of the seven kings who besieged Thebes, who held God in contempt and holds him in contempt still on the burning sand.

entities.name: Brunetto
entities.body: Ser Brunetto Latini, the Florentine scholar who taught Dante how man makes himself eternal, and whom Dante finds among the sodomites.

entities.name: Priscian
entities.body: A grammarian named among the clerks on the burning sand.

entities.name: Francesco d’Accorso
entities.body: A Bolognese jurist named among the clerks on the burning sand. Longfellow calls him Francis of Accorso.

entities.name: Guido Guerra
entities.body: A Florentine of great worth, grandson of the good Gualdrada, one of the three who circle on the burning sand. Longfellow writes the name as one word, Guidoguerra.

entities.name: Gualdrada
entities.body: The Florentine woman named as Guido Guerra’s grandmother.

entities.name: Tegghiaio
entities.body: Tegghiaio Aldobrandi, whose counsel Florence should have heeded.

entities.name: Jacopo Rusticucci
entities.body: A Florentine who blames his savage wife for his ruin, one of the three on the burning sand.

entities.name: Guglielmo Borsiere
entities.body: A Florentine newly arrived in Hell, who has been telling the others how the city has changed.

entities.name: Vitaliano
entities.body: A Paduan usurer, expected in Hell by the one already there.

entities.name: Venedico
entities.body: Venedico Caccianemico, a Bolognese who sold his own sister to the Marquis.

entities.name: Ghisola
entities.body: Venedico’s sister, whom he persuaded to satisfy the Marquis.

entities.name: Jason
entities.body: The leader of the Argonauts, punished as a seducer for Hypsipyle and Medea.

entities.name: Hypsipyle
entities.body: The woman Jason deceived and abandoned on Lemnos.

entities.name: Medea
entities.body: The woman Jason abandoned after Hypsipyle.

entities.name: Alessio Interminei
entities.body: A flatterer of Lucca, sunk in filth.

entities.name: Thais
entities.body: The harlot of Terence’s comedy, named as the last of the flatterers.

entities.name: Simon Magus
entities.body: The man who tried to buy the power of the Holy Spirit, and gave his name to the sin punished in the third ditch.

entities.name: Nicholas
entities.body: Pope Nicholas the Third, planted head downward in the rock, who mistakes Dante for the pope who will succeed him.

entities.name: Boniface
entities.body: Pope Boniface the Eighth, whom Nicholas mistakes Dante for and expects to take his place head-down in the rock.

entities.name: Clement
entities.body: The pope from the west who will come after Boniface, a lawless shepherd.

entities.name: Constantine
entities.body: The emperor whose gift to the first wealthy Father is named as the root of the Church’s corruption.

entities.name: Sylvester
entities.body: The pope Constantine sought out at Soracte to cure his leprosy.

entities.name: Amphiaraus
entities.body: One of the seven against Thebes, swallowed by the earth; now a diviner walking backwards.

entities.name: Tiresias
entities.body: The Theban seer who changed from man to woman and back, among the diviners.

entities.name: Aruns
entities.body: An Etruscan diviner of the hills of Luni.

entities.name: Manto
entities.body: Tiresias’s daughter, the virgin seer who settled where Mantua now stands; Virgil tells her story to correct the legend of his own city.

entities.name: Eurypylus
entities.body: The augur who with Calchas cut the first cable at Aulis.

entities.name: Calchas
entities.body: The Greek augur of the Trojan war.

entities.name: Michael Scot
entities.body: The Scottish astrologer, thin in the flanks, who knew every trick of magical illusion.

entities.name: Guido Bonatti
entities.body: An astrologer of Forlì, among the diviners.

entities.name: Asdente
entities.body: A cobbler of Parma turned soothsayer, who now wishes he had stuck to his leather.

entities.name: The elder of Santa Zita
entities.body: The barrator of Lucca whom a demon carries in and throws into the pitch.

entities.name: The Navarrese
entities.body: The barrator born in the kingdom of Navarre, who tricks the demons into letting him dive.

entities.name: Fra Gomita
entities.body: A friar of Gallura, a vessel of every fraud, who sold his master’s enemies their freedom.

entities.name: Don Michel Zanche
entities.body: A barrator of Logodoro in Sardinia.

entities.name: Catalano
entities.body: A Jovial Friar of Bologna, one of the two hypocrites in leaden capes who governed Florence together.

entities.name: Loderingo
entities.body: A Jovial Friar of Bologna, Catalano’s partner in governing Florence.

entities.name: The one pinned to the ground
entities.body: The high priest who counselled that one man should suffer for the people, crucified across the path of the hypocrites.

entities.name: Vanni Fucci
entities.body: A thief of Pistoia, a mule of a man, who robbed the sacristy and let another man be blamed.

entities.name: Cacus
entities.body: The centaur who guards the thieves, whose thefts by fraud set him apart from his brothers.

entities.name: Cianfa
entities.body: A Florentine thief, transformed into a six-footed serpent.

entities.name: Agnello
entities.body: A Florentine thief, fused with the serpent that attacks him.

entities.name: Buoso
entities.body: A Florentine thief, changed into a serpent as the poet watches.

entities.name: Buoso Donati
entities.body: The dead man whom Gianni Schicchi impersonated in order to forge a will.

entities.name: Puccio
entities.body: A Florentine thief, the only one of the five who was not transformed.

entities.name: Ulysses
entities.body: The Greek whose cunning took Troy, and who tells of his last voyage beyond the pillars of Hercules; he burns in a double flame with Diomedes.

entities.name: Diomedes
entities.body: Ulysses’s companion, burning in the same flame. Longfellow spells him Diomed.

entities.name: Deidamia
entities.body: Achilles’s bride, who still mourns him; the cunning that took him from her is part of what Ulysses burns for.

entities.name: Guido
entities.body: Guido da Montefeltro, the soldier turned friar, damned for advising Boniface to promise much and keep little.

entities.name: Messer Guido
entities.body: Guido del Cassero, one of the two best men of Fano, warned of drowning off La Cattolica.

entities.name: Angiolello
entities.body: One of the two best men of Fano, warned with Guido del Cassero.

entities.name: Mahomet
entities.body: The founder of Islam, cleft from chin to belly among the sowers of discord.

entities.name: Ali
entities.body: Cleft in the face, walking weeping before Mahomet.

entities.name: Fra Dolcino
entities.body: The heretic leader whom Mahomet sends a warning to arm himself with food.

entities.name: Pier da Medicina
entities.body: A sower of discord with his throat pierced and his nose cut away, who sends the warning to Fano.

entities.name: Curio
entities.body: The shade with his tongue cut out, who urged Caesar across the Rubicon.

entities.name: Mosca
entities.body: Mosca dei Lamberti, whose counsel — "a thing done has an end" — began the Guelf and Ghibelline split in Florence.

entities.name: Bertran de Born
entities.body: The troubadour who carries his own severed head like a lantern, punished for setting a son against his father.

entities.name: Geri del Bello
entities.body: Dante’s kinsman, seen pointing at him in anger because his death is unavenged.

entities.name: Alberto
entities.body: Alberto of Siena, who had the Aretine alchemist burned for a joke about flying.

entities.name: Capocchio
entities.body: An alchemist who falsified metals, and a good ape of nature.

entities.name: Gianni Schicchi
entities.body: The Florentine who impersonated the dead Buoso Donati to forge a will and take the best mare in the stud.

entities.name: Myrrha
entities.body: The shade who disguised herself to lie with her own father, running mad beside Gianni Schicchi.

entities.name: Master Adam
entities.body: The counterfeiter of Florentine coin, swollen with dropsy, who dreams of the streams of the Casentino.

entities.name: Guido
entities.body: One of the Counts of Romena, for whom Master Adam counterfeited, and whose soul he longs to see in the ditch.

entities.name: Alessandro
entities.body: One of the Counts of Romena, named with his brother Guido.

entities.name: The false woman who accused Joseph
entities.body: Potiphar’s wife, burning with fever beside Sinon.

entities.name: Sinon
entities.body: The Greek who talked Troy into taking in the horse, burning with fever.

entities.name: Bocca
entities.body: Bocca degli Abati, the traitor of Montaperti, who refuses to give his name until Dante tears at his hair.

entities.name: Camicion
entities.body: Camicion de’ Pazzi, frozen in Caina, who names the traitors around him and awaits his kinsman Carlino.

entities.name: Carlino
entities.body: The kinsman whose worse treachery Camicion says will excuse his own.

entities.name: Albert
entities.body: The father of the two brothers of the Bisenzio valley, frozen face to face in Caina.

entities.name: The one Arthur pierced
entities.body: The traitor whose breast and shadow were broken by one blow of his own father’s hand.

entities.name: Focaccia
entities.body: A traitor of Pistoia named among the frozen.

entities.name: Sassol Mascheroni
entities.body: A Florentine traitor named among the frozen.

entities.name: Gianni del Soldanieri
entities.body: A Florentine traitor in the ice; Longfellow drops the final vowel.

entities.name: Ganelon
entities.body: The betrayer of Roland at Roncesvalles. Longfellow spells him Ganellon.

entities.name: Tebaldello
entities.body: The man who opened Faenza’s gates while the city slept.

entities.name: Ugolino
entities.body: Count Ugolino della Gherardesca, who gnaws the head of the archbishop who starved him and his children in the tower.

entities.name: Ruggieri
entities.body: Archbishop Ruggieri of Pisa, who locked Ugolino and his sons in the tower and threw away the key.

entities.name: Anselm
entities.body: One of Ugolino’s children in the tower, who asks his father why he stares.

entities.name: Gaddo
entities.body: One of Ugolino’s children, who falls at his father’s feet in the tower.

entities.name: Uguccione
entities.body: One of Ugolino’s children in the tower.

entities.name: Brigata
entities.body: One of Ugolino’s children in the tower.

entities.name: Alberigo
entities.body: Friar Alberigo, who served the fruit at his own treacherous banquet, and whose soul is in Hell while his body still walks the world.

entities.name: Branca d’Oria
entities.body: A Genoese whose soul has been in the ice for years while a devil wears his body.

entities.name: Judas
entities.body: The betrayer of Christ, head-first in Lucifer’s central mouth.

entities.name: Cassius
entities.body: Caesar’s assassin, hanging from one of Lucifer’s black jaws.

entities.name: Christ
entities.body: The Redeemer, named in Paradise and referred to in Hell only by circumlocution.

entities.name: Mary
entities.body: The mother of Christ, the gracious Lady who first moved to help Dante and who receives the last prayer of the poem.

entities.name: Peter
entities.body: Saint Peter, keeper of the keys of Heaven; his gate and his seat recur throughout.

entities.name: Paul
entities.body: The apostle whose journey to the third heaven Dante names beside Aeneas’s as precedent.

entities.name: The Baptist
entities.body: John the Baptist, the patron Florence adopted in place of Mars.

entities.name: Lucia
entities.body: Saint Lucy, the enemy of all cruelty, who sends Beatrice to Dante’s aid and carries him while he sleeps.

entities.name: Rachel
entities.body: Jacob’s wife, seated beside Beatrice among the blessed and a figure of the contemplative life.

entities.name: Adam
entities.body: The first father, drawn out of Limbo by the Harrowing.

entities.name: Eve
entities.body: The first mother, who took the bitter fruit from the serpent.

entities.name: Abel
entities.body: Adam’s son, drawn out of Limbo by the Harrowing.

entities.name: Noah
entities.body: Drawn out of Limbo by the Harrowing.

entities.name: Moses
entities.body: The lawgiver, drawn out of Limbo by the Harrowing.

entities.name: Abraham
entities.body: The patriarch, drawn out of Limbo by the Harrowing.

entities.name: David
entities.body: The psalmist king, drawn out of Limbo by the Harrowing.

entities.name: Israel
entities.body: Jacob, drawn out of Limbo with his father and his children.

entities.name: Cain
entities.body: The first murderer; the man in the moon carrying thorns is called by his name.

entities.name: Michael
entities.body: The archangel who took vengeance on the proud rebellion.

entities.name: Elijah
entities.body: The prophet taken up in the chariot of fire.

entities.name: Elisha
entities.body: The prophet who watched Elijah’s chariot depart.

entities.name: Joseph
entities.body: The patriarch falsely accused by Potiphar’s wife.

entities.name: Caesar
entities.body: Julius Caesar, seen armed in Limbo and named through the poem as the founder of the empire.

entities.name: Augustus
entities.body: The emperor under whom Virgil lived.

entities.name: Scipio
entities.body: The Roman who became the heir of glory by routing Hannibal.

entities.name: Hannibal
entities.body: The Carthaginian routed by Scipio.

entities.name: Charlemagne
entities.body: The emperor whose rout at Roncesvalles cost him his holy campaign.

entities.name: Roland
entities.body: The paladin whose horn sounded at Roncesvalles.

entities.name: Robert Guiscard
entities.body: The Norman conqueror in Apulia, whose wars left bones still gathered on the field.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: The chief of the pagan gods, whose thunderbolt and whose blacksmith are invoked.

entities.name: Juno
entities.body: The goddess whose rage against the Theban house drove Athamas mad.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: The god of war, Florence’s first patron before the Baptist.

entities.name: Neptune
entities.body: The god of the sea.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The god of poetry, invoked at the opening of the Paradiso.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The goddess of the moon and the hunt.

entities.name: Minerva
entities.body: The goddess of wisdom.

entities.name: Bacchus
entities.body: The god of wine; Thebes is called his city.

entities.name: Latona
entities.body: The mother of Apollo and Diana, who gave birth on Delos.

entities.name: The Muses
entities.body: The goddesses of poetry, invoked at the outset of each canticle.

entities.name: Circe
entities.body: The enchantress who kept Ulysses near Gaeta for more than a year.

entities.name: Phaethon
entities.body: The boy who dropped the reins of the sun’s chariot and scorched the sky.

entities.name: Arachne
entities.body: The weaver turned spider, named for the pattern of Geryon’s hide.

entities.name: Narcissus
entities.body: The boy who pined at his own reflection; his mirror is the water Master Adam thirsts for.

entities.name: Theseus
entities.body: The Duke of Athens who killed the Minotaur, and whom the Furies wish they had punished.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The hero whose club ended Cacus, and whose pillars mark the limit Ulysses passed.

entities.name: Deianira
entities.body: The woman Nessus died for.

entities.name: Semele
entities.body: The Theban woman whose love of Jove brought Juno’s rage on her house.

entities.name: Athamas
entities.body: The king driven mad by Juno, who killed his own son.

entities.name: Hecuba
entities.body: Troy’s queen, who went mad with grief and howled like a dog.

entities.name: Polydorus
entities.body: Hecuba’s son, found dead on the seashore.

entities.name: Polyxena
entities.body: Hecuba’s daughter, whose death she saw.

entities.name: Charybdis
entities.body: The whirlpool whose waves crash and break, likened to the clash of the hoarders and spenders.

entities.name: Icarus
entities.body: The boy whose wings failed him, named when Dante rides down on Geryon.

entities.name: Daedalus
entities.body: Icarus’s father, who called to him as the wax melted.

entities.name: Atropos
entities.body: The Fate who cuts the thread.

entities.name: Epicurus
entities.body: The philosopher whose followers held that the soul dies with the body, and whose cemetery is the sixth circle.

entities.name: The Florentines
entities.body: Dante’s own city and its people, the subject of more of the poem’s anger than any other.

entities.name: The Trojans
entities.body: The people of Troy, from whose survivors Rome descends.

entities.name: The Greeks
entities.body: The people who took Troy.

entities.name: The Romans
entities.body: The people of the empire Virgil sang and Dante defends.

entities.name: The Jews
entities.body: Named in the ditch of the hypocrites and in the sowing of evil seed.

entities.name: The Christians
entities.body: Named in the poem’s reproaches to the living.

entities.name: The Pharisees
entities.body: The council that took counsel against Christ.

entities.name: The Saracens
entities.body: Named among the enemies the papacy did not make war on.

entities.name: The Cherubim
entities.body: An order of angels; one of the black Cherubim claims Guido da Montefeltro.

entities.name: The Seraphim
entities.body: The highest order of angels.

entities.name: The Thebans
entities.body: The people who saw the earth open for Amphiaraus.

entities.name: The Sienese
entities.body: A people the poem calls the vainest in the world.

entities.name: The Bolognese
entities.body: Named in the ditch of the panders.

entities.name: The Genoese
entities.body: A people at odds with every virtue, in the poem’s judgment.

entities.name: The Lombards
entities.body: The people of Virgil’s parents.

entities.name: The Mantuans
entities.body: The people of Virgil’s city.

entities.name: The Tuscans
entities.body: The people of Dante’s region.

entities.name: The Aretines
entities.body: The people of Arezzo.

entities.name: The Paduans
entities.body: The people of Padua.

entities.name: The French
entities.body: Named beside the Sienese for vanity.
